newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks close at new six-year high.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks close at new six-year high.

text.p: Taiwan share prices fought off profit-taking on Wednesday to close higher for the seventh consecutive session and set a six-year high, but brokers said market momentum was slowing.
The weighted index ended 13.63 points or 0.18 percent higher at 7,424.10. That surpassed the 7,410.47 close on Tuesday, and was the market's highest finish since it ended at 7,857.01 on June 2, 1990.
Turnover was a hectic T$101.42 billion.
Constructions and electronics led the gains, rising 3.22 percent and 1.50 percent respectively.
But the heavily weighted financials slumped 0.82 percent, while recently hot plastics and textiles dropped 0.42 percent and 0.41 percent respectively.
"Constructions benefited from profit-taking in other sectors like plastics and textiles, which are hitting a strong resistance," said Eric Liu, analyst for National Securities.
"But the index will find good support as long as investors are willing to put their money somewhere else in the market rather than just sell and leave," Liu said.
Ruentex Construction soared by the daily seven-percent limit or T$1.40 to T$21.90.

Taiwan Semiconductor, the island's biggest chipmaker, gained T$4 to close at T$62 after it announced on Tuesday that its net profit for 1996 rose by 28.6 percent, despite a global plunge in chip prices.
Electronic shares also were boosted by hopes for high dividends in the dividend-issue season that starts in March, brokers said.
Brokers expected the index to consolidate at the current level on Thursday. A 7,380-7,460 range was seen.
